title: csoai.fix-receipt/0.1
description: A fix receipt records that a named fault was measured before a named change, measured again after it, and what the two measurements support. It is the fourth verb beside find, name and remedy: prove a fix held. A receipt is a statement about THIS estate's own faults. It is never a statement about anybody else's system, never a conformity mark, and nothing in it is offered for sale. The measurements are what carry the weight; the verdict is a label derived from them under verdict_rule and carries no authority of its own.
publisher: Council of AI (CSOAI Ltd, UK Companies House 16939677)

chain_id.description: The chain this receipt belongs to. A receipt is only ordered within its own chain.

seq.description: Position in the chain, from 0. seq 0 is the GENESIS link and carries no measurement.

prev_hash.description: The state_digest of the previous link; 64 zeros at seq 0. A removed or reordered receipt breaks this.

state_digest.description: sha256 of THIS link with the state_digest key removed, canonicalised as json.dumps(link, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True). Recomputable from the published line alone: an edited receipt fails its own digest even if prev_hash still lines up. See digest_rule in the README.

receipt_id.description: FR-YYYY-MMDD-NN. Stable; a superseding receipt gets a new id and names the one it supersedes.

supersedes.description: receipt_id this one supersedes. Signed or published bytes are never edited; a wrong receipt is superseded.

ref.description: Where the fault is recorded: a corrections ledger id, a lane report path, an evidence bundle, a log line. At least one must be something a reader can fetch or reproduce.

source.description: Who or what found it. 'this estate' is a real answer and so is an external correspondent.

scope_note.description: The fault as scoped for THIS receipt. A receipt that measures a narrower thing than the fault must say so here, because the verdict then applies only to the narrow thing.

kind.description: NONE is legitimate: a fault can close because the world moved. It is never evidence of a fix on its own.

change.description: What was done. A landed commit is a change, not a fix: the measurements decide.

verdict.description: VERIFIED_FIX: both measurements exist, are comparable, and moved in the direction expected_direction names. FIX_FAILED: both exist and the value did not move that way. PARTIAL: the scoped remedy is measurably working while the fault it addresses is measurably still present. UNVERIFIABLE: at least one side cannot be measured — no stated change, no instrument, a destroyed before-state, or an effect that is not observable from outside. UNVERIFIABLE is a first-class outcome and is the honest label for most fixes; recording it is the point of this artifact, not a failure of it.

verdict_rule.description: The one sentence that derives the verdict from before and after. If this sentence cannot be written, the verdict is UNVERIFIABLE.

expected_direction.description: Stated BEFORE the after-measurement wherever possible: which way the value had to move for the fix to have held.

state.description: PUBLISHED: a live /api/corrections entry. DRAFT_IN_APPROVE_QUEUE: written to the owner's approve-queue and not published; only the owner promotes. NONE: no corrections entry is owed, and the receipt says why.

residual.description: What is still wrong after the change, including faults that are NOT this fault. null only when nothing is known to remain. A VERIFIED_FIX with a residual is common and must not be read as 'working'.

not_established.description: What this receipt does not prove. Always populated. A receipt establishes a measured change of state and nothing else: not the absence of other faults, not the quality of the remedy, and never a conformity statement about anyone.

contents.description: GENESIS only: what the chain is and what it covers.

what.description: The quantity or state measured. One quantity per receipt; two quantities are two receipts.

value.description: The reading. Any JSON type. null ONLY with state UNMEASURED or UNMEASURABLE.

method.description: How it was read, in enough detail to repeat. A method nobody can repeat makes the side UNMEASURABLE.

source.description: The bytes the reading came from.

state.description: MEASURED: a reading was taken. UNMEASURED: not measured, though it could have been. UNMEASURABLE: no instrument can take this reading now — a destroyed before-state, an effect not observable from outside. Either non-MEASURED state forces verdict UNVERIFIABLE.

by.description: Who took the reading. A reading taken by the party that made the change is worth less than one taken by anybody else, and saying which it was is part of the reading.
